en.title: Maximum Last Element After Rearranging and Only Decreasing
en.description:
You may rearrange the array arbitrarily and decrease elements to integers of at least 1. The final first element must be 1, and a[i]−a[i−1]≤1 must hold for i≥1; find the maximum value of the last element. This is a one-sided difference condition, and the original array need not be sorted.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the array. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 1≤element≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 4, 1 and 2. A single element must become 1; you cannot simply take the maximum as the answer.
hints: After sorting, start with current=0 and update current=min(v,current+1) for each value v; the final current is the answer.
